F5.answer1: Explainability refers to the representation of the mechanisms underlying AI systems' operation, which helps users understand how these systems function internally. Interpretability, on the other hand, pertains to the meaning of AI systems' output in the context of their designed functional purposes, aiding users in understanding what the outputs mean within their specific contexts. Together, these concepts assist operators and overseers of AI systems, as well as end-users, in gaining deeper insights into the functionality and trustworthiness of the system, including its outputs. This combination reduces negative risk perceptions that arise from a lack of ability to make sense of or contextualize system output appropriately. Developers and deployers are encouraged to test various transparency tools to ensure AI systems are used as intended, enhancing both explainability and interpretability.
F5.answer2: Explainability refers to a representation of the mechanisms underlying AI systems' operation, while interpretability pertains to the meaning of AI systems' output in the context of their designed functional purposes. Together, these characteristics help operators, overseers, and users understand the functionality and trustworthiness of AI systems more deeply. Perceptions of negative risk often arise from an inability to appropriately contextualize system outputs, which is why explainable and interpretable AI systems are beneficial. Transparency, explainability, and interpretability are distinct but complementary characteristics that support each other, with explainability addressing how decisions were made within the system.
F5.query: What is the difference between explainability and interpretability?
